inputs.original_text: Earlier this month, an Indiana judge blocked a pro-life law after the American Civil Liberties Union and Hoosier Jews for Choice argued it burdened the ability to obtain an abortion in accordance with sincerely held beliefs. This looks like a coordinated reframing: turn abortion access into a religious-rights shield so legal limits can be portrayed as attacks on faith. LifeNews.com’s title—“This Judge Thinks Killing Babies in Abortions is a Religious Right”—makes clear how sharply the ruling is being presented, but the larger move is to make a contested policy harder to challenge by wrapping it in religious freedom.
inputs.modified_text: This ruling looks less like a straightforward religious-freedom dispute and more like a carefully chosen way to make abortion limits politically untouchable. The ACLU and Hoosier Jews for Choice argued that the Indiana law burdened abortion access tied to sincerely held beliefs, and now the fight can be recast as the state attacking faith. LifeNews.com’s inflammatory title pushes the opposite framing, but both sides’ messaging helps turn a contested policy into a battle over religious identity—exactly the kind of framing that shields the underlying agenda from scrutiny.
